top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct measurement principle (many neutral atoms interrogated with the light shift cancelled) from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes, and it has been experimentally verified: independent laboratories reproduce uncertainties near 10^-18, compare clocks across sites, resolve millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and bound varying constants and dark-matter couplings. Katori (invention and first realisation) and Ye (systematic control and many-body clock physics) carry the concentrated credit; the citation must name the lattice concept, not precision in general. Unresolved priority questions for other groups are a real cost but do not outweigh awarding a mature, reproduced achievement over no award.
